input: Draft a parenting agreement with my co-parent

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: A parenting agreement can range from a simple informal outline to a comprehensive legal document covering custody schedules, holidays, finances, education, healthcare, and more — knowing what topics to include shapes the entire structure.

The number of children, their ages, and any special needs directly determine which clauses are necessary — e.g., a toddler needs different provisions than a teenager with school and extracurricular commitments.
Whether this is for a divorce, separation, or an unmarried co-parenting arrangement affects the legal framing and whether it needs to be filed with a court.
If the agreement must meet a court's requirements or be reviewed by a lawyer, that sets hard limits on format, language, and what must be included or excluded.

Knowing the intended format — a ready-to-sign formal document, a structured draft to take to a mediator, or a bullet-point working outline — determines how polished and detailed the output needs to be.
The tone of the agreement (cooperative and informal vs. legally precise and formal) reflects the relationship dynamic between co-parents and affects how it will be received and used.
Understanding which issues are already agreed upon vs. still in dispute helps prioritize what the draft needs to resolve or leave flexible, and signals what 'done' looks like.

gold.taskDescription: Create a written parenting agreement between the user and their co-parent covering custody, responsibilities, and other shared parenting terms.

questions.title: Which topics must the agreement cover?
questions.description: Identify the specific areas to include — such as physical custody schedule, legal decision-making, holidays, child support, education, healthcare, or travel rules.

questions.title: How many children, and what are their ages?
questions.description: Capture the number of children involved and their ages, as this drives which provisions (school schedules, medical needs, extracurriculars) are relevant.

questions.title: Is this tied to a divorce, separation, or informal arrangement?
questions.description: Determine the legal and relationship context so the agreement uses the right framing and accounts for any court involvement.

questions.title: Does this need to be court-compliant or lawyer-ready?
questions.description: Clarify whether the document must meet specific legal standards, will be filed with a court, or is purely a private agreement between the two parties.

questions.title: What format do you need — full draft or working outline?
questions.description: Determine whether the output should be a polished, near-final document or a structured draft to be refined with a mediator or attorney.

questions.title: Should the tone be formal legal language or plain collaborative wording?
questions.description: Establish the preferred tone and style so the document reflects the co-parents' relationship dynamic and communication preferences.

questions.title: Which issues are already agreed on vs. still unresolved?
questions.description: Identify where both parties are aligned and where gaps remain, so the draft can lock in settled terms and flag areas that still need negotiation.
